t: You're looking at a statue of William Ewart Gladstone in Bow, made by the Irish sculptor Albert Bruce-Joy, who worked in England. Gladstone was prime minister four separate times between 1868 and 1894, more than anyone else in the job. He began as a Conservative and ended as the face of the Liberal Party. He was also Chancellor of the Exchequer four times and an MP for over sixty years, so his career spans almost the whole Victorian era.
